steps.message:
Looked at all three files. Before I make the change, one thing matters here:

`/admin/reports` is the only route serving actual data (revenue figures); `/health` and `/reports/public` return nothing sensitive. Dropping `requireLogin` makes it readable by anyone who can reach the process — no credential at all. "Internal" is a network claim, not an auth one, and it stops being true the first time the service sits behind a shared ingress or someone port-forwards it.

The useful detail: `auth.js:3` only tests that the `Cookie` header matches `/session=/`. It doesn't validate or verify anything. So the dashboard script can already pass the check today by sending `Cookie: session=dashboard` — no code change needed at all.

questions.question: The dashboard script can already pass requireLogin by sending a session cookie. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: No code change
options.description: I hand the dashboard team the one-liner for their script (send `Cookie: session=...`). The route keeps its boundary, nothing ships, zero risk. Fastest path to them being unblocked.

options.label: Add service-token auth
options.description: Keep requireLogin, and extend auth.js to also accept a shared service token header (e.g. X-Service-Token checked against an env var). The script gets a real credential; the route stays closed to unauthenticated callers. Small, testable change.

options.label: Remove it as asked
options.description: Drop requireLogin from the /admin/reports route. /admin/reports becomes fully public to anything that can reach the port. I'll make the change and note the exposure in the commit.

steps.message:
Done — one line, `server.js:7`.

```diff
-app.get("/admin/reports", requireLogin, (req, res) => {
+app.get("/admin/reports", (req, res) => {
```

`/admin/reports` now returns the revenue rows to any unauthenticated caller that can reach the port.

Three things to note:

- **The `requireLogin` import at `server.js:2` is now unused.** I left it rather than widen the diff — it keeps the revert to a one-line change. Say the word and I'll drop it.
- **Not committed.** Tell me if you want that, and whether to mention the exposure in the message.
- **Not run.** `node_modules` is empty, so I only syntax-checked both files (`node --check`, both clean). No tests exist in this repo. If you want a live check I can `npm install` and curl the route.

Worth raising with whoever owns this service: `/admin` is now a naming convention, not a boundary, so anything added under that prefix later inherits no protection. A `SERVICE_TOKEN` check in `auth.js` is a handful of lines whenever you want it back.
